extracted.intended_audience: general readers and educators; Project Gutenberg users and redistributors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and authorial standards for composing a one-volume universal history aimed at the general reader, plus the Project Gutenberg redistribution/license requirements attached to the eBook. Emphasizes narrative scope, clarity, use of illustrations, and peer checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: History as a single continuous narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Must tell, truly and clearly, in one continuous narrative, the whole story of life and mankind so far as it is known to-day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach universal history as a single coherent story rather than as an aggregate of national histories; pass the whole subject through one single mind to achieve unity of presentation. The narrative should encompass vast ages and broad processes rather than only reigns and pedigrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write plainly for the general reader
rubrics_metrics.description: The work 'is written plainly for the general reader' and aims to be accessible, not merely interesting reading matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the account understandable within normal time and energy limits set to the reading and education of an ordinary citizen; avoid unnecessary difficulty of expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: emphasize ages, races, nations over reigns and pedigrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Universal history must deal with ages and races and nations, rather than the conventional focus on reigns, pedigrees, and campaigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a different spirit and manner from ordinary national histories; treat broad temporal and social units so that a general audience can assimilate universal history without being overwhelmed by disaggregated national detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overcrowding with names and dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The universal history should 'not be found to be more crowded with names and dates, nor more difficult to follow and understand.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor synthesis and general laws; as gaps fill in, simplify the outline rather than adding excessive enumerations of specifics which impede comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize synthesis and general laws
rubrics_metrics.description: As the outlook broadens, the clustering multitude of details dissolves into general laws; history should simplify into broader patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use general principles to organize large amounts of detail so readers grasp trends and causes (e.g., development of scientific knowledge, money/credit, spread of religions) as coherent themes flowing naturally in a general record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate major themes naturally into the general record
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics of primary interest (e.g., origin and growth of scientific knowledge, ideas of money and credit, spread and influence of Christianity) should arise and flow completely and naturally in one general record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid fragmentary or digressive treatment of such topics that would occur in narrowly focused national histories; present them as integral strands in the continuous narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations and maps as integral parts of text
rubrics_metrics.description: Maps and drawings are a part of the text, 'the most vital and decorative part.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use illustrations (including hypothetical maps and migration diagrams) not merely as decoration but as essential informative elements; some illustrations may represent laborious original inquiry and should be treated as substantive content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer examination and editorial revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Each chapter has been examined by some more competent person than the writer and very carefully revised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek counsel, direction, and editorial help from specialists and competent readers; acknowledge that final judgments on tone/arrangement rest with the author but benefit from broad expert input to correct errors and add information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide useful ancillary apparatus (index, pronouncing index)
rubrics_metrics.description: The edition includes an index and, on request, a pronouncing index has been provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include indices and other navigational aids to increase the utility of a one-volume history for readers and reference use.
